Even without touching the clocks my card is now boosting to 1905mhz on its own and holding it rock steady under heavy load, which is something I never saw on the air cooler, and aside from the tiny whirring noise from my pump and a very faint hum from my fans my PC is so quiet you can barely hear it even sitting right next to it.

As a fun sciencey follow-up, RDNA has a terrible habit of not being able to hold lower FPS at Freesync and/or V-SYNC levels. I play more than a dozen games that my 6900XT can push well above the 170 FPS at 1440p of my display, but by capping at that setting, I save nearly 100W off the GPU draw. Worth it! 

However, this is a double edged sword as the AMD driver/vbios does it's best to minimize clock speeds if the Core isn't at 100% load, and in some cases, even if it is at 100% load. Minecraft, Deep Rock Galactic, and at least a dozen others all can't maintain their FPS stability, or in some cases, even refuse to clock up at all (particularly minecraft!) resulting in some cripplingly low performance from something that should be running at 400fps. 

My old 1060 Max-Q Dell laptop runs Minecraft at 2-3x the FPS of my Strix G15 6800M OR my desktop's 5600X+6900XT... tell me what doesn't look right here lol.

I know there's been much said about AMD's renewed focus on gaming but I'm just going to point out that the hardware here is still great for rendering I think the main issue is software.

AMD's OpenCL rendering pipeline for Blender (and other softwares) was once superior to CUDA (in part thanks to AMD's memory bandwidth) but their support for it has stagnated as Nvidia has made big software strides with Blender(CUDA) and is now even advancing onward to OPTIX which is once again another leap in performance on the same hardware.


There's so much performance to be had with an updated/supported pipeline and I think that's where AMD is currently lacking. AMD's hardware is not being leveraged in Blender as you'd expect.
author: @OGPatriot03

text: One of the big reasons is the lack of software support. AMD's GPGPU implementation - HIP - is not supported by desktop software. AMD is moving away from OpenCL, but most software focuses on NVIDIA's CUDA with OpenCL as an afterthought, and no mention of HIP. They were slapped in the face when Blender dropped OpenCL, and rushed to get HIP working on Windows for the release of Blender 3.0. Linux support is still not great either, and they're playing catch-up in terms of overall features. AMD just doesn't have the resources to compete in both fields at once, and they're clearly focusing their GPU efforts on gaming right now.
